query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a nanocrystalline grain structure in single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys will enhance coercivity through grain boundary pinning.
generation.conditions: Grain size in the nanoscale range (e.g., 50-100 nm)
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary pinning of magnetic domain walls
generation.predicted_outcome: Enhanced coercivity (Hc) compared to single-phase fcc FeCoNi
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi with coarse grain structure
generation.boundary: Grain size limit (e.g., 50-100 nm) for effective grain boundary pinning
generation.uncertainty: Optimal grain size and distribution for maximum coercivity enhancement

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of magnetic properties (Hc, Ms) between single-phase fcc FeCoNi with coarse grain structure and nanocrystalline grain structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the nanocrystalline sample is not significantly higher than that of the coarse-grained sample, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The saturation magnetization (MS) and coercivity (Hc) for the four different samples analyzed in the present study have been listed in Table 1. The MS of AlCoFeNi is substantially higher compared to that of the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy for both heat-treated conditions. While the magnetization is primarily determined by composition and the crystal structure, the coercivity can be affected by impurities, deformation, grain size and phase decomposition. The coercivity (Hc) decreased with increasing annealing temperature from 15 Oe for sample aged at 600 °C/15 h, exhibiting nanoscale phase separation, to 4 Oe for samples aged at 1000 °C/15 h, exhibiting a homogeneous undecomposed B2 matrix. A similar observation has been reported in the literature, where the coercivity of the AlCoCrCuFeNi HEA annealed at 1000 °C/2 h decreases by 30 Oe (from 45 Oe to 15 Oe) compared to as-cast alloys. The AlCoFeNi HEA investigated in the present study exhibits higher saturation magnetization and lower coercivity than other soft ferrite magnetic materials, e.g., MnZn ferrite, Cu-Zn-Ti ferrite,, as revealed in Supplementary Table 2.

Another complementary, but top-down method which influences the microstructure and therefore the magnetic properties is the High-Pressure Torsion (HPT) process. It yields not only a grain refinement down to the nanoscale, but also can initiate various phase transformations, such as the formation or decomposition of supersaturated solid solutions, dissolution of phases, formation of nanocrystals during decomposition of amorphous phases or amorphization of crystalline phases [,,,]. Consequently, HPT can be used to tailor the magnetic properties by for example locally changing the alloy composition, yielding a pronounced grain refinement and strained grain interfaces as well as an increase in dislocation density [,]. The grain size can be reduced until a certain value, the saturation grain size. The typical saturation grain size for alloys and HEAs reported in the literature is in the range of 50–100 nm [,,]. Recently, the effect of the HPT process on the saturation grain size and mechanical properties has been investigated for the Cantor alloy system [,].
